_notes: FULL-COVERAGE DUMMY 1099-INT — every one of the 61 writable boxes on Drake's INT
screen carries a value, so one run proves the whole map at once. The only box left
out is field 14, the payer's foreign province, which is a '<Click to Access>'
sub-screen and not typeable at all.
The amounts are deliberately distinct and nothing like a real statement — 1000, 21,
3300, 440 ... — so every box on the screenshot can be traced back to the field that
wrote it. This is a TEST RETURN payload. It is not anybody's tax data.
The country boxes (15, 26) take a two-letter CODE, not a country name. Typing CANADA
made Drake match on the first two letters and drop the rest, so the run refused to
commit it. Whether CA is Canada on Drake's list is a HUMAN's call from the dropdown —
read it on the screenshot; the agent can only prove the code was accepted.
Fields 1, 3, 4 and 12 are CONFIRMED dropdowns as of 2026-08-12 — a live run read each
one back as the typed code plus the entry Drake selected, and the value was then
readable on the form. Fields 15, 26, 34, 37, 58 and 61 are still unmeasured. A Drake
dropdown with no matching entry accepts the typing, echoes it in the heads-down popup
and stores NOTHING, so the per-field gate passes and the box stays empty. The FORM
CHECK at the end of the run is what catches that. Expect some of those six to be
reported missing — that is the measurement, not a failure.
Client: the test return 123456789 / fynn, Test.
federal_code is '0' because that is the ONLY thing Drake accepts in that box besides
blank ('0' excludes the item from the federal return). On a real return nobody should
be setting it from an extraction — it is a preparer's election. It is here so the box
is proven, on a test return where excluding the item costs nothing.
